general_rules.rule: Always animate label text and its high-contrast container pill as a single atomic unit so text never appears partially faded without full backing contrast.

reference_gaps: Jared Owen: Unlike Jared Owen's continuous physical mechanics and spatial camera moves linking macro and micro views, this film hard-cuts between flat slide-like diagrams with multi-second static holds (00:00-00:03, 00:37-00:40) and omits core physical geometry like prism refraction and Earth's day/night terminator.

Animagraffs: Unlike Animagraffs' dense, precise visual craftsmanship and cleanly anchored callouts, this film relies on generic stock-like shapes (magnifying glass, stick figure, blobby cropped Earth) with a misanchored caliper bracket (00:12) and low-contrast fading text labels (00:18, 00:32, 00:35, 00:42).

The Why Side: Unlike The Why Side's bold visual state changes every 2-4 s and razor-tight VO-to-picture sync, this film stalls on a 3-second opening title hold, desyncs captions across the end card (00:40-00:42), and holds the final orbital diagram nearly motionless for 3 seconds.

mg-styles-15 Flat Vector (7.6 anchor): Unlike the benchmark's anticipation, squash-and-stretch, 2-4 frame staggers, crisp flat shapes, and element-driven shape-wipe transitions, this film uses soft radial-blur glows, raw linear opacity label fades, repetitive diagonal sheen wipes, and rigid un-eased icon entrances.
strengths: Clear, intuitive 5-chapter conceptual arc ("your sunset is the leftovers of someone else's blue sky") with a well-structured wave-scatter comparison at 00:14-00:17.
Clean loop return at 00:42-00:46 that settles back onto the opening sunset horizon and whips horizontally into frame 0 with matching audio whoosh.
Strong editorial instinct to include genuine NASA ISS documentary proof (00:32-00:33), clean VO loudness/clarity, and an effective signature musical sting on "That's the mechanism."
Clean stage framing (zero boxed-frame failures) and a consistent blue/navy/amber brand palette across most body segments.
summary: Sky_v8 has a clear conceptual arc, clean VO loudness, and a solid loop whip into frame 0, but it lands firmly in template/slide-deck territory (5-6 across craft dimensions) and requires ONE MORE PASS. Three blockers prevent shipping: (1) label text repeatedly fades in separately from its dark backing pill, causing unreadable ~1.04 contrast ghosts (00:18, 00:32, 00:35, 00:42); (2) captions desync across the end card so "the mechanism." pops up over the returning sunset at 00:42 after the card is gone; and (3) the climactic orbital sunset sequence feels like clipart (left-cropped Earth with no day/night terminator, 3 s near-static hold) while burying the awe-inspiring real NASA ISS sunset photo in a cluttered 1.5 s flash. Tightening hook pacing, adding physical depletion/terminator accuracy, unifying atomic label entrances, replacing synthetic UI pings with organic foley, and building a true match-cut hero moment into the ISS photo will elevate this above the 7+ professional bar.

weaknesses.fix: Bind label text and its dark backing pill inside one atomic <Label> component so backdrop opacity hits 1.0 on frame 1 of visibility; animate the unified pill in over 6 frames using scale(0.88 -> 1.04 -> 1.0) with cubic-bezier(0.22, 1.25, 0.36, 1) and >=32 px type at >=7:1 contrast.
weaknesses.issue: Multiple labels fade their text in independently of their dark pill containers, producing unreadable low-contrast ghost text ("BLUE 0×" at 00:18, "NASA ISS028-E-007274" at 00:32, "SOMEONE ELSE'S AFTERNOON" at 00:35, "SAME LIGHT, LATER" at 00:42) — confirmed by measured QA contrast min_ratio=1.04 and labels_persist=False.

weaknesses.fix: WOW-FACTOR FIX: Center Earth cleanly inside x: 90-990 px with a crisp flat-vector day/night terminator shadow (#0A1328 at 55% opacity) and layered atmospheric limb; animate a continuous camera glide along the grazing beam from noon across the terminator into sunset as blue photons peel off and the surviving beam thins and shifts #FFFFFF -> #FFB020 -> #FF5A36, then match-cut on the curved glowing horizon directly into a 3.5 s hold on the NASA ISS photo (4% slow scale drift) with at most two clean badges ("SEEN FROM THE ISS" top-left, credit pill at y <= 1140 px).
